newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CDU denies received Elf funds.
newsitem.headline: German CDU denies received Elf funds.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) have not received funds from France's Elf-Aquitaine, a party spokesman said on Tuesday, denying a French media report.
"Funds from the French oil company Elf-Aquitaine have not flowed to the CDU directly or indirectly, contrary to allegations in French media reports," CDU spokesman Rolf Kiefer said in a statement.

The newspaper Le Parisien said Elf paid a 13.5 million mark ($7.8 million) commission to a Liechtenstein-based company -- Noblepac -- in connection with its purchase of the former East German petrochemicals combine Leuna and the Minol petrol station network.
Noblepac is owned by Andre Guelfi, an intermediary who is already under judicial investigation in the case.

Le Parisien said Noblepac transferred the funds further, mainly to Germany, including to the CDU via an unnamed Bavarian intermediary, and that a magistrate wanted to trace the recipients of the money.

Justice sources in Paris said a French magistrate investigating alleged corruption by former executives of the Elf Aquitaine oil company has been authorised to extend her probe to suspect payments involving Germany.
The public prosecutor's office on Monday gave judge Eva Joly permission to investigate alleged covert commission paid in 1992 in connection with Elf's purchase of Leuna, the sources said.

Elf bought both Leuna and Minol from a German government agency (Treuhandanstalt) in charge of privatising the former communist state's industries. The investigation concerns suspected offences of misuse of corporate funds.
A spokesman for Elf in Paris declined comment on the report, while Elf officials in Germany were unavailable.
The Paris spokesman said a new refinery the company was building at Leuna, near Leipzig, as part of the deal, would be operational later this year.

The Elf case began as an investigation of alleged financial irregularities when Loik Le Floch-Prigent was chairman in 1988-93. It has since widened to cover Elf's operations and commission payments abroad, including dealings in Gabon and Venezuela.
